description: Cross-binding conformance for esm-spec §6.6.2 'Unrecognized override keys': every `parameter_overrides` key must designate exactly ONE parameter of the flattened system, and a key that designates none is an ERROR — not a silently-ignored no-op. Three outcomes are pinned, and they are DISTINCT: a key that resolves (exactly, or by the local spelling §6.6 mandates) runs; a BARE key that is the local name of two or more parameters is AMBIGUOUS; anything else is UNKNOWN. Ambiguous is kept apart from unknown because the fixes differ — qualify the name versus correct it — and because silently binding one of two candidates would be a wrong answer rather than a missing one. Rust already raised `SimulateError::InvalidParameter` for the unknown case; Julia and Python silently ignored it, so an author's override did nothing and the run still reported a verdict. This category is what keeps the three from drifting apart again: unlike the other categories it compares DIAGNOSTIC OUTCOMES, not numbers, so it carries no golden — each binding's runner asserts its own idiomatic error type per case.

scope_excluded.go: rewrite-only port; no simulator, so no override-key surface
scope_excluded.typescript: rewrite-only port; no simulator, so no override-key surface

error_surface._comment: The idiomatic error each binding raises per outcome. The TYPE is per-language; the OUTCOME classification is the cross-binding contract.

cases.note: Exact hit on the flattening-qualified name.
The LOCAL spelling §6.6 mandates, unique across the document. The non-vacuity anchor: a binding that rejected every bare key would fail here.
Two components carry this local name; binding either would be a wrong answer.

A DOTTED key resolves only under rule 2, which needs its trailing segment to be a parameter name outright; here the parameter is `Left.solo`, not `solo`, so rule 2 fails. Rule 3 is for BARE keys only, so the qualifier is never discarded and `Missing.solo` does not quietly become `Left.solo` — an author who names a component that does not exist is told so.

fixtures._trajectory_comment: `Left.x` integrates (Left.gain + Left.solo) and `Right.y` integrates Right.gain, both from 0 over [0,1], so a resolved override is VISIBLE at t=1 and a binding that accepted a key without actually binding it is caught too. The RHS is constant, so every solver reproduces these within the manifest tolerance.
